questions.question: In a triangle PQR, ∠PQR = 90°, PQ = 10 cm and PR = 26 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of inradius of incircle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Triangle PQR is a right-angled triangle at Q (∠Q = 90°).

Given PQ = 10 cm and PR = 26 cm (Hypotenuse).

Using Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13) × 2 → (10, 24, 26). Thus, QR = 24 cm.

Inradius (r) of a right triangle = (Base + Perpendicular − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2

r = (10 + 24 − 26) ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perpendicular (PQ) = 10 cm

Hypotenuse (PR) = 26 cm

**Formula Used:**

Third side (QR) = √(PR² − PQ²)

Inradius (r) = Area ÷ Semi-perimeter (s)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1b0ad269f497d6eb1447fe598456f8e5b678355b5eb419239d1d16d71085e07.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ QR = √(26² − 10²)

⇒ QR = √(676 − 100) = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ Area = 0.5 × 24 × 10 = 120 cm²

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (10 + 24 + 26) ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm

⇒ Inradius (r) = Area ÷ s = 120 ÷ 30

⇒ r = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The circumradius (R) of a right-angled triangle is equal to half of its hypotenuse: R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2.

General Inradius Formula

For any triangle, the inradius r is given by Area (A) ÷ Semi-perimeter (s), where s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) help in solving right triangle problems faster.</p

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠A = 58°. If I is the in-centre of the triangle, then the measure of ∠BIC is∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Angle at the in-centre (I) is always given by: ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2)

Given ∠A = 58°

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (58° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + 29° = 119°

**∴ The correct answer is 119°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In ΔABC, ∠A = 58°

I is the in-centre of the triangle.

**Formula Used:**

In any triangle, the angle formed by the internal bisectors of two angles at the in-centre is 90° plus half of the third angle: ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9aaebb4e97215e46780e759746f46905f2dd324530271d46c8d22361a6233c1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠A = 58°

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + (58° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠BIC = 90° + 29°

⇒ ∠BIC = 119°

**∴ The correct answer is 119°.**

**__Additional Information__**

In-centre Properties

The in-centre is the intersection of the internal angle bisectors. The radius of the in-circle (r) = Area ÷ semi-perimeter (s).

Circumcentre Angle

If O is the circumcentre of ΔABC, then the angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠A.

Orthocentre Angle

If H is the orthocentre of ΔABC, then the angle ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A.

Ex-centre Angle

If Iₑ is the ex-centre opposite to vertex A, then the angle ∠BIₑC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2).</p

questions.question: S is the incentre of ΔPQR. If ∠PSR = 125°, then the measure of ∠PQR is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In any triangle, the angle at the incentre is 90° + half of the vertical angle.

∠PSR = 90° + (∠PQR / 2)

125° = 90° + (∠PQR / 2)

35° = ∠PQR / 2 ⇒ ∠PQR = 35° × 2 = 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

S is the incentre of ΔPQR and ∠PSR = 125°.

**Formula Used:**

The angle subtended by a side at the incentre S is given by 90° + (opposite vertex angle / 2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/971eca7b8a3180065461a40a06c8c2125ac6fbc79255e5ce488057cec226e90c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠PSR = 90° + (∠PQR / 2)

⇒ 125° = 90° + (∠PQR / 2)

⇒ ∠PQR / 2 = 125° − 90°

⇒ ∠PQR / 2 = 35°

⇒ ∠PQR = 35° × 2

⇒ ∠PQR = 70°

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Excentre Angle Property

The angle formed at the excentre (E) opposite to vertex Q is ∠PER = 90° − (∠Q / 2).

Circumcentre Angle Property

The angle subtended by side PR at the circumcentre O is exactly twice the angle at vertex Q: ∠POR = 2 × ∠PQR.

Inradius Formula

The radius of the incircle (r) is given by r = Area of triangle (Δ) ÷ Semi-perimeter (s).

Incentre Definition

The incentre is the point where the three internal angle bisectors of a triangle intersect and it is equidistant from all sides.</p

questions.question:
In ΔXYZ, G is the centroid. If XY = 11 cm, YZ = 14 cm and XZ = 7 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of GM?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9241eefd455150d6518676da02e184aa3ed436f156aedd821acc202fe8349f53.png]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a triangle, the length of median XM = 1/2 √(2(XY² + XZ²) − YZ²).

Given XY = 11, XZ = 7, YZ = 14.

XM = 1/2 √(2(11² + 7²) − 14²) = 1/2 √(2(121 + 49) − 196) = 1/2 √(340 − 196).

XM = 1/2 √144 = (1/2) × 12 = 6 cm.

Centroid G divides median XM in ratio XG : GM = 2 : 1, so GM = (1/3) × XM.

GM = (1/3) × 6 = 2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Triangle XYZ with sides XY = 11 cm, YZ = 14 cm, and XZ = 7 cm. G is the centroid and XM is the median to side YZ.

Formula Used: Apollonius Theorem ⇒ 2(XM² + YM²) = XY² + XZ², where M is the midpoint of YZ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc9bbce40b2d51512ac375baa81fee175c68cdfa2887f9588423c1603e9b7336.png] 

⇒ M is the midpoint of YZ, so YM = YZ ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.

⇒ By Apollonius Theorem: 2(XM² + 7²) = 11² + 7²

⇒ 2(XM² + 49) = 121 + 49

⇒ 2(XM² + 49) = 170

⇒ XM² + 49 = 85

⇒ XM² = 85 − 49 = 36

⇒ XM = √36 = 6 cm

⇒ Centroid G divides median XM such that XG : GM = 2 : 1

⇒ GM = 1/(2 + 1) × XM = 1/3 × 6 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Centroid Property

The centroid of a triangle is the intersection point of its three medians and divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex.

Apollonius Theorem

For any triangle with sides a, b, c and median mₐ to side a: b² + c² = 2(mₐ² + (a/2)²).

Median Area Property

The three medians divide the triangle into six smaller triangles of equal area.</p

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 35 cm and 37 cm. What is the circumradius of the triangle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the sides: 12, 35, 37. These form a Pythagorean triplet since 12² + 35² = 144 + 1225 = 1369 = 37².

For any right-angled triangle, the circumradius (R) is equal to half of the hypotenuse.

The longest side is the hypotenuse = 37 cm.

R = 37 ÷ 2 = 18.5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.5 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the triangle: a = 12 cm, b = 35 cm, c = 37 cm.

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, Circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35c5c8265c7ea6832981483497751b59a81d86d6cbdfe2557241efda0880653c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, verify if the triangle is right-angled using Pythagoras theorem.

⇒ a² + b² = 12² + 35²

⇒ a² + b² = 144 + 1225 = 1369

⇒ c² = 37² = 1369

⇒ Since a² + b² = c², the triangle is a right-angled triangle where the longest side (37 cm) is the hypotenuse.

⇒ Circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

⇒ R = 37 ÷ 2

⇒ R = 18.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18.5 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inradius of a Right-Angled Triangle

The inradius (r) of a right-angled triangle can be calculated as r = (Perpendicular + Base − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Circumcenter Location

In a right-angled triangle, the circumcenter always lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse and is equidistant from all three vertices.

General Circumradius Formula

For any triangle with sides a, b, c and area A, the circumradius R = (a × b × c) ÷ (4 × A).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), (8, 15, 17), (9, 40, 41), and (12, 35, 37).</p

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in quadrilateral ABCD touching AB, BC, CD and AD at the points P, Q, R and S, respectively, and ∠B = 90°. If AD = 24 cm, AB = 27 cm and DR = 6 cm, then what is the circumference of the circle?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Tangents from an external point are equal: DR = DS = 6 cm. AS = AD − DS = 24 − 6 = 18 cm, and AP = AS = 18 cm. PB = AB − AP = 27 − 18 = 9 cm. Since angle B = 90⁰, the radius r of the inscribed circle is equal to PB = 9 cm. Circumference = 2 × π × r = 2 × π × 9 = 18π. **∴ The correct answer is 18π cm.**

questions.question: O is the circumcenter of the isosceles ΔABC. Given that AB = AC = 5 cm and BC = 6 cm. The radius of the circle is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of the isosceles triangle (h) = √(5² − (6/2)²) = √(25 − 9) = 4 cm.

Area of triangle (A) = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm².

Circumradius (R) = (Product of all sides) ÷ (4 × Area).

R = (5 × 5 × 6) ÷ (4 × 12) = 150 ÷ 48 = 3.125 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.125 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB = AC = 5 cm, BC = 6 cm. Triangle ABC is isosceles. O is the circumcenter.

**Formula Used:** Circumradius (R) = (a × b × c) / (4 × Area)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ad813f3b72d5251e2edd3b37c257e209cd11f6f5e116e08804705f3a71432fb.png] 

⇒ Let AD be the altitude from A to BC. Since ABC is isosceles, D is the midpoint of BC.

⇒ BD = DC = BC ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.

⇒ In right-angled ΔABD, AD = √(AB² − BD²) = √(5² − 3²) = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4 cm.

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm².

⇒ Circumradius (R) = (AB × AC × BC) ÷ (4 × Area)

⇒ R = (5 × 5 × 6) ÷ (4 × 12) = 150 ÷ 48

⇒ R = 3.125 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.125 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumradius of Equilateral Triangle

For an equilateral triangle with side 'a', the circumradius (R) is given by R = a / √3.

Circumradius of Right-Angled Triangle

In a right-angled triangle, the circumradius (R) is exactly half of the hypotenuse (R = h / 2).

Relation between R and Area

For any triangle with sides a, b, c and area K, the circumradius R = abc / 4K and the inradius r = K / s, where s is the semi-perimeter.</p

questions.question: ABC is an equilateral triangle. If the area of the triangle is 36√3, then what is the radius of circle circumscribing the triangle ABC ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × side² = 36√3

⇒ side² = 36 × 4 = 144 ⇒ side = 12

Direct Formula: Circumradius (R) = side / √3

⇒ R = 12 / √3 = 4√3

**∴ The correct answer is 4√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of equilateral triangle ABC = 36√3

**Formula Used:**

1. Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × a² (where a is the side)

2. Circumradius (R) of equilateral triangle = a / √3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af0375dc969168c00f3e4b0940e5bfc75a2443d9dbd253cccfc92d9a5bf7d024.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × a² = 36√3

⇒ a² = (36√3 × 4) / √3

⇒ a² = 144

⇒ a = √144 = 12

⇒ Circumradius (R) = a / √3

⇒ R = 12 / √3

⇒ R = (4 × 3) / √3

⇒ R = 4√3

**∴ The correct answer is 4√3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inradius of Equilateral Triangle

The radius of the incircle (r) is given by r = a / (2√3). It is exactly half of the circumradius (R = 2r).

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The altitude or height (h) is given by h = (√3 / 2) × a. Note that h = R + r = 3r.

Area in terms of Height

The area of an equilateral triangle can also be calculated as Area = h² / √3.</p

questions.question: If O is the orthocentre of ΔABC and ∠BOC = 100°, the measure of ∠BAC is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In any triangle, the angle formed by the orthocentre at the base side is supplementary to the opposite vertex angle.

Property: ∠BOC + ∠BAC = 180°

Given: ∠BOC = 100°

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 100° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Triangle ΔABC with orthocentre O.

Angle ∠BOC = 100°.

**Formula:**

The angle subtended by a side at the orthocentre (O) is: ∠BOC = 180° − ∠A (where ∠A is the vertex angle ∠BAC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ced151bbaf13a1ddcb58f4650641621f26e1cbbd64383b0089ca6ee840044c24.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔABC, let O be the intersection of altitudes AD and BE.

⇒ In quadrilateral AF OE (where F and E are feet of altitudes on AB and AC), ∠F = ∠E = 90°.

⇒ Since sum of angles in a quadrilateral is 360°, ∠A + ∠FOE = 180°.

⇒ ∠FOE = ∠BOC (Vertically opposite angles).

⇒ ∴ ∠A + ∠BOC = 180°.

⇒ 100° + ∠A = 180°.

⇒ ∠A = 180° − 100°.

⇒ ∠A = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Circumcentre Angle Property

If O is the circumcentre of ΔABC, then the angle subtended at the centre is double the angle at the circumference: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC.

Incentre Angle Property

If I is the incentre of ΔABC, the angle BOC is given by the formula: ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2).

Excentre Angle Property

If E is the excentre opposite to vertex A, the angle formed is: ∠BEC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2).</p

questions.question: In triangle PQR, the internal bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet at O. If ∠QPR = 70°, then what is the value of ∠QOR?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the internal bisectors of two angles of a triangle at the incenter O is given by the formula:

∠QOR = 90° + (∠P ÷ 2)

Given ∠P = 70°

∠QOR = 90° + (70° ÷ 2) = 90° + 35° = 125°

**∴ The correct answer is 125°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠QPR = 70°, O is the intersection of internal bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R.

**Formula:** Angle at the incenter ∠QOR = 90° + (∠P / 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97f213fde9f258bc8bd5eefabd26c2ba55c16bacfe660cfda264b44383321add.png] 

⇒ In ΔPQR, ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180°

⇒ ∠Q + ∠R = 180° − 70° = 110°

⇒ Divide by 2: (∠Q/2) + (∠R/2) = 55°

⇒ In ΔOQR, ∠QOR + ∠OQR + ∠ORQ = 180°

⇒ ∠QOR + (∠Q/2) + (∠R/2) = 180°

⇒ ∠QOR + 55° = 180°

⇒ ∠QOR = 180° − 55° = 125°

**∴ The correct answer is 125°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Incenter Properties

The incenter is the point of intersection of internal angle bisectors and is equidistant from all sides of the triangle.

External Bisector Angle

The angle formed by external bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R is given by: 90° − (∠P / 2).

Circumcenter Angle

The angle formed by the sides at the circumcenter is twice the angle at the opposite vertex: ∠QCR = 2 × ∠P.</p
